devanagari: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । / न चाति स्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥6.16॥
iast: nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ । / na cāti svapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna ॥6.16॥
sayIt: NAAT-yush-na-tus-too YO-go-sti na chai-KAAN-ta-ma-NUSH-na-taha / na CHAA-ti svup-na-SHEE-lus-ya JAA-gra-to NY-va CHAAR-joo-na
translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who stays always awake, Arjuna.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: for one who eats too much
for one who does not eat at all
for one in the habit of too much sleep
for one who stays always awake

meaning: Before any technique, Krishna sets a precondition: moderation. Meditation does not work for a person swinging between extremes — overeating or starving, oversleeping or refusing rest. The verse is strikingly practical: yoga is not built on heroic deprivation any more than on indulgence, and both extremes damage the instrument you practise with, the body-mind itself. Commentators across Advaita, Vishishtadvaita, and Dvaita traditions agree on the call to balance and differ mainly over how the right measure is fixed — by scriptural guideline or by what keeps the body fit for practice — without disputing the point itself. This verse states the problem in the negative; the next verse, 6.17, gives the positive prescription.
reflection: Which extreme — too much or too little — is quietly unbalancing your practice right now?

devanagari: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । / युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥6.17॥
iast: yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu । / yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā ॥6.17॥
sayIt: yook-TAA-haa-ra-vi-HAA-rus-ya yook-ta-CHESH-tus-ya KAR-ma-soo / yook-ta-svup-NAA-va-BO-dhus-ya YO-go BHA-va-ti dooh-kha-HAA
translation: For one measured in food and recreation, measured in effort in all actions, measured in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: for one whose food and recreation are measured
whose sleep and waking are measured

meaning: The positive half of the moderation teaching: when food, recreation, effort in work, sleep, and waking are all yukta — yoked to the right measure — yoga becomes "the destroyer of sorrow." The claim is bold: a regulated ordinary life is not a boring preamble to spiritual practice; it is what makes practice actually relieve suffering. For daily use, pick the one input most out of measure — usually sleep or food — and adjust it slightly rather than heroically. Traditions read the goal differently — Advaita hears a mind steadied for liberating knowledge, while Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita hear a discipline sustaining meditation on the Lord — but all agree the doorway is moderation.
reflection: Where could one measured adjustment — in food, rest, or work — reduce your daily friction?

devanagari: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । / योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥6.19॥
iast: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā । / yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ ॥6.19॥
sayIt: ya-THAA DEE-po ni-VAA-tus-tho NENG-ga-tay so-pa-MAA smri-TAA / YO-gi-no ya-ta-CHIT-tus-ya YOON-ja-to yo-ga-MAAT-ma-naha
translation: As a lamp standing in a windless place does not flicker — that is the simile recalled for the yogi of restrained mind, practising the yoga of the self.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: One of the Gita's most loved images: a lamp flame in a windless place does not flicker — that, the verse says, is the traditional simile for the mind of a disciplined yogi absorbed in the yoga of the self. The image teaches by contrast with our ordinary state, where every draught of thought, worry, and news bends the flame. Notice what the simile does not promise: the wind is not abolished; the lamp is simply placed where wind cannot reach it. Daily practice is largely the craft of building that windless place — a regular time, a seat, a closed door — and then letting the flame stand still on its own.
reflection: What would a windless place look like in your day — and when could you sit in it?

devanagari: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । / ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥6.26॥
iast: yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram । / tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet ॥6.26॥
sayIt: ya-TO ya-TO nish-CHA-ra-ti ma-nush-CHUN-cha-la-mus-THI-rum / ta-tus-ta-TO ni-yum-YAI-ta-DAAT-mun-YAY-va VA-shum na-yet
translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders off, from precisely there let one rein it in and bring it back under the control of the self alone.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.26, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: The most forgiving instruction in the chapter. The mind is called cañcala and asthira — restless and unsteady — as a statement of fact, not a scolding. The practice is simply this: wherever the mind wanders off, from precisely there bring it back, and bring it back again. Every wandering is another repetition of the exercise, not proof of failure. Where the mind is to be brought — "into the self" — is read differently: Advaita hears resting the mind in the one Self, awareness itself, while Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita hear fixing it on the Lord as the object of meditation, and the verse gives room to both. What no tradition disputes: returning, without drama, is the whole technique.
reflection: The next time your mind wanders today, can you bring it back once, without scolding it?

devanagari: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । / ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥6.29॥
iast: sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani । / īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ ॥6.29॥
sayIt: sar-va-BHOO-tus-tha-MAAT-maa-num sar-va-BHOO-taa-ni CHAAT-ma-ni / EEK-sha-tay yo-ga-yook-TAAT-maa SAR-va-tra sa-ma-DAR-sha-naha
translation: One whose self is joined in yoga, seeing the same everywhere, sees the self present in all beings and all beings in the self.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.29, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: one whose self is joined in yoga

meaning: The fruit of the discipline: the yogi whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, looking on everything with an equal eye. Practically, the verse turns meditation outward — the steadiness won on the seat becomes a way of seeing people. Here the traditions genuinely part ways: Advaita reads literal identity, one Self appearing as all; Vishishtadvaita reads all beings as forming the body of the one Brahman; Dvaita reads the Lord dwelling within every being — likeness, not identity — and this verse is a touchstone for each. What all three share is the demand it makes: no one you meet stands outside what you revere.
reflection: Who did you meet today in whom you did not look for the same self that is in you?

devanagari: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । / तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥6.30॥
iast: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati । / tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati ॥6.30॥
sayIt: yo MAAM PUSH-ya-ti SAR-va-tra SAR-vum cha MA-yi PUSH-ya-ti / tus-YAA-hum na pra-nush-YAA-mi sa cha may na pra-NUSH-ya-ti
translation: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees everything in me — to him I am never lost, and he is never lost to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.30, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: A promise of mutual presence: whoever sees the divine everywhere, and everything within the divine, is never lost to it — and it is never lost to them. The language turns intimate here; this is no longer a technique but a relationship that, once genuine, cannot be dropped from either side. Traditions hear the "me" differently: Advaita takes it as the universal Self, so the verse describes never falling out of one's own true nature, while Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita hear Krishna speaking personally, pledging that the devotee and the Lord never lose each other — and both readings live in the same words. For daily practice, try looking at one ordinary thing as held inside something greater.
reflection: What ordinary thing could you look at today as held within the divine?

devanagari: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । / सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥6.32॥
iast: ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo'rjuna । / sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ ॥6.32॥
sayIt: aat-MOW-pum-YAY-na SAR-va-tra SA-mum PUSH-ya-ti YOR-joo-na / SOO-khum vaa YA-di vaa DOOH-khum sa YO-gee PA-ra-mo ma-taha
translation: One who sees the same everywhere by comparison with himself, Arjuna — whether in joy or in sorrow — that yogi is held to be the highest.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.32, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: A definition of the highest yogi that has nothing to do with feats of meditation: it is the one who measures everyone by their own self — who feels another's joy and pain as they feel their own. The Sanskrit ātmaupamyena, "by comparison with oneself," makes empathy a spiritual instrument, not a soft skill. The verse guards the whole chapter against a cold reading: mastery of the mind that does not widen into fellow-feeling has missed the point. For daily practice it is a portable test — before responding to anyone today, ask how the situation would land if it were yours. The person who lives that way, the verse says, is parama: supreme.
reflection: Whose joy or pain today can you measure by asking how it would feel as your own?

devanagari: श्रीभगवानुवाच / असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् । / अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥6.35॥
iast: śrībhagavānuvāca / asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam । / abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate ॥6.35॥
sayIt: shree-bha-ga-VAA-noo-VAA-cha / a-SUM-sha-yum ma-HAA-BAA-ho MA-no door-NI-gra-hum cha-lum / abh-YAA-say-na too kown-TAY-ya vy-RAAG-yay-na cha GRIH-ya-tay
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to restrain; but by practice, son of Kunti, and by dispassion, it is grasped.
source: Bhagavad Gita 6.35, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: is grasped, is brought to hold

meaning: Arjuna has just protested that controlling the mind is harder than controlling the wind, and Krishna's reply begins with full agreement: asaṃśayam — "no doubt about it." The mind really is hard to restrain. Then come the two tools: abhyāsa, repeated practice, and vairāgya, dispassion — the slow release of the cravings that keep dragging the mind out. This is the Gita's whole psychology of habit in one line, and it is deliberately encouraging: the difficulty is admitted, and the method still works. For daily life, keep the pair together — practice without loosening your grasping burns out, and detachment without practice drifts. Small repetitions, gently held, win.
reflection: What small practice could you repeat tomorrow, even though your mind resisted it today?

devanagari: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । / तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥9.22॥
iast: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate । / teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ॥9.22॥
sayIt: a-nun-YAASH chin-ta-YUN-toh maam yay ja-NAAH par-yoo-PAA-sa-tay / tay-SHAAM nit-YAA-bhi-yook-TAA-naam yo-ga-KSHAY-mum va-HAAM-ya-hum
translation: Those who worship me with undivided attention, thinking of nothing else — for those ever-steadfast people I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
source: Bhagavad Gita 9.22, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: with no other (object of thought), undivided
worship fully, attend on every side
gaining what is lacking and keeping what is gained

meaning: This is one of the Gita's plainest promises. To the person whose attention is undivided — who keeps returning to the divine rather than splitting loyalty across a hundred anxieties — Krishna says: I take over the logistics. Yoga-kṣema is an old compound for the two things worry feeds on: getting what you don't yet have, and protecting what you do. The verse does not promise a life without effort; it promises that steady devotion is met, that the carrying is shared. Devotional traditions treasure this verse as a guarantee of divine care; a sober daily reading is simpler — practise steadiness first, and let the accounting anxieties loosen their grip.
reflection: Which worry about getting or keeping could you set down today, and hand over?

devanagari: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । / तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥9.26॥
iast: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati । / tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ॥9.26॥
sayIt: PUT-rum POOSH-pum PHA-lum TOH-yum yoh may BHAK-tyaa pra-YUCH-cha-ti / ta-DA-hum bhak-tyoo-pa-HRI-tum ush-NAA-mi pra-ya-TAAT-ma-nah
translation: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion — that offering of love from a person of pure heart, I accept.
source: Bhagavad Gita 9.26, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: of one whose self is pure, disciplined

meaning: The verse behind the everyday offering. What reaches the divine is not the price of the gift but the devotion it is carried with — a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a cup of water are enough, and Krishna says he accepts them personally. The one qualifier is prayata-ātmanaḥ: the offerer's heart is clean, the giving sincere. This is the scriptural root of the simple home puja practised across Hindu households, where whatever is at hand becomes an offering. For daily practice it lowers every barrier: you do not need wealth, ritual expertise, or a temple. You need one small thing, given with full attention.
reflection: What small, ordinary thing could you offer today with your whole attention?

devanagari: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । / यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥9.27॥
iast: yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat । / yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam ॥9.27॥
sayIt: yut ka-ROH-shi ya-dush-NAA-si yuj joo-HOH-shi da-DAA-si yut / yut ta-PUS-ya-si kown-TAY-ya tut koo-ROOSH-va ma-DAR-pa-num
translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, O son of Kunti — do it as an offering to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 9.27, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: Where 9.26 blessed the small formal offering, this verse dissolves the boundary between worship and everything else. Work, meals, giving, discipline — the whole texture of an ordinary day — can be turned into offering by a shift of intention. Nothing new is added to the to-do list; what changes is the direction the action faces. This is the seed of what later devotional traditions systematise as arpaṇa or dedicating the fruits of action, and it pairs naturally with 2.47: act fully, release the result, and here, hand the result somewhere. For daily practice, pick one routine act — cooking, commuting, a meeting — and do it consciously as an offering.
reflection: Which routine act today will you quietly turn into an offering?

devanagari: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । / ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥9.29॥
iast: samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ । / ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham ॥9.29॥
sayIt: sa-MO-hum sar-va-BHOO-tay-shoo na may DVAYSH-yo-sti na pri-yah / yay bha-JUN-ti too maam BHAK-tyaa MA-yi tay TAY-shoo CHAAP-ya-hum
translation: I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me and none is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
source: Bhagavad Gita 9.29, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: and I too am in them

meaning: Hold both halves honestly, because the verse itself does. The first half declares complete divine impartiality: no favourites, no enemies. The second half says devotees live "in me, and I in them" — which sounds exactly like favouritism. Commentators resolve the tension in different ways rather than one settled reading: a common traditional analogy is fire, which is the same for everyone but warms those who come near; devotional schools stress that the mutual indwelling is real reciprocity, freely open to anyone who turns toward it. Either way, the practical point survives every reading: access is not rationed by birth, status, or past — nearness is created by turning.
reflection: If divine warmth is the same for all, what one step of turning toward it will you take today?

devanagari: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । / मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥9.34॥
iast: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru । / māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ ॥9.34॥
sayIt: mun-ma-NAA BHA-va mud-BHUK-toh mud-YAA-jee maam na-mus-KOO-roo / maa-may-VIGH-shya-si yookt-VIGH-vum aat-MAA-num mut-pa-RAA-ya-nah
translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer worship to me, bow to me. Having joined yourself to me in this way, with me as your highest aim, you will come to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 9.34, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: one who offers worship to me
with me as your highest aim, final refuge

meaning: The closing verse of chapter nine compresses devotional practice into four verbs: think, love, worship, bow. Mind, heart, action, and body each get an instruction, so devotion is not left as a vague feeling — it is a full-person orientation you can actually do. The promise attached is direct: joined this way, you come to me. Nearly the same words return at 18.65 with a personal vow added, a sign of how central the Gita considers this instruction. For daily practice, take the four verbs literally and small: a thought turned toward the divine, a moment of warmth, one act done as worship, one physical bow.
reflection: Of the four — think, love, worship, bow — which one is missing from your day, and when will it happen?

devanagari: अर्जुन उवाच / एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते । / ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥12.1॥
iast: arjuna uvāca / evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate । / ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ ॥12.1॥
sayIt: ar-JOO-na oo-VAA-cha / AY-vam sa-ta-ta-YOOK-taa yay bhak-TAAS-tvaam par-yoo-PAA-sa-tay / yay CHAAP-yak-sha-ram av-YAK-tam TAY-shaam kay yo-ga-VIT-ta-maah
translation: Arjuna said: Those devotees who worship you with such constant steadiness, and those who worship the imperishable and unmanifest — which of them understands yoga best?
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.1, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: Arjuna opens the chapter on devotion with a practical question: who has the better grasp of yoga — the person who worships God as a personal presence with steady devotion, or the one who contemplates the formless, imperishable absolute? It is the question anyone building a practice eventually faces: do I direct my attention to a form I can love, or to a truth beyond all form? The chapter that follows is Krishna's answer. Traditions weigh that answer differently: Advaita readers tend to see worship of the personal form as a support on the way to formless realisation, while Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita readers hold personal devotion to be the highest path in itself.
reflection: Which comes easier to you — the divine with a face, or the truth beyond form?

translations.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: जो भक्त इस तरह निरंतर आपसे जुड़े रहकर आपकी उपासना करते हैं, और जो अविनाशी, अव्यक्त की उपासना करते हैं — इन दोनों में योग को सबसे अच्छा कौन जानता है?

meanings.hi: भक्ति के अध्याय की शुरुआत अर्जुन एक व्यावहारिक सवाल से करते हैं: योग की बेहतर समझ किसे है — उसे जो ईश्वर को एक व्यक्तिगत उपस्थिति मानकर स्थिर भक्ति से पूजता है, या उसे जो निराकार, अविनाशी परम तत्व का चिंतन करता है? यह वह सवाल है जो साधना गढ़ने वाले हर व्यक्ति के सामने कभी न कभी आता है: मैं अपना ध्यान किसी ऐसे रूप पर टिकाऊँ जिसे प्रेम कर सकूँ, या रूप से परे किसी सत्य पर? आगे का पूरा अध्याय कृष्ण का उत्तर है। परंपराएँ उस उत्तर को अलग-अलग तौलती हैं: अद्वैत की दृष्टि में सगुण रूप की उपासना निराकार अनुभूति की ओर एक सहारा है, जबकि विशिष्टाद्वैत और द्वैत के लिए व्यक्तिगत भक्ति अपने आप में सर्वोच्च मार्ग है।

devanagari: श्रीभगवानुवाच / मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । / श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥12.2॥
iast: śrībhagavānuvāca / mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate । / śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ ॥12.2॥
sayIt: shree-bha-ga-VAAN oo-VAA-cha / mai-YAA-vaysh-ya MA-no yay maam nit-ya-YOOK-taa oo-PAA-sa-tay / shrad-dha-YAA pa-ra-yo-PAY-taas-tay may yook-ta-ta-MAA ma-TAAH
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, always steady and filled with the highest faith — these I consider the most accomplished in yoga.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.2, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: most fully disciplined, most accomplished in yoga

meaning: Krishna gives a direct answer to Arjuna's question: those who fix the mind on him personally, worship with constancy, and bring the highest faith are, in his view, the most accomplished in yoga. Notice the three ingredients — attention (the mind fixed), consistency (always steady), and trust (supreme faith). For a daily practice, this is a workable checklist: not intensity on one heroic day, but a mind that keeps returning, day after day, with confidence in what it returns to. Traditions differ on the verse's scope: bhakti schools such as Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita read it as ranking personal devotion supreme, while Advaita reads it as praising the more accessible path rather than the final truth.
reflection: What would trusting your practice completely look like today?

translations.hi: श्रीभगवान ने कहा: जो अपना मन मुझमें एकाग्र करके, सदा स्थिर रहकर, परम श्रद्धा के साथ मेरी उपासना करते हैं — उन्हें मैं योग में सबसे श्रेष्ठ मानता हूँ।

meanings.hi: अर्जुन के प्रश्न का कृष्ण सीधा उत्तर देते हैं: जो मन को उनके व्यक्तिगत रूप पर टिकाते हैं, निरंतरता से उपासना करते हैं और परम श्रद्धा लेकर आते हैं, वे उनकी दृष्टि में योग में सबसे सिद्ध हैं। तीन तत्वों पर ध्यान दीजिए — ध्यान (टिका हुआ मन), निरंतरता (सदा स्थिर रहना) और भरोसा (परम श्रद्धा)। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए यह एक काम की सूची है: किसी एक वीर दिन की तीव्रता नहीं, बल्कि ऐसा मन जो दिन-प्रतिदिन लौटता रहे, और जिस पर लौटता है उस पर भरोसा रखे। श्लोक के दायरे पर परंपराओं में मतभेद है: विशिष्टाद्वैत और द्वैत जैसी भक्ति-परंपराएँ इसे व्यक्तिगत भक्ति को सर्वोच्च ठहराने के रूप में पढ़ती हैं, जबकि अद्वैत इसे अंतिम सत्य नहीं, बल्कि अधिक सुलभ मार्ग की प्रशंसा मानता है।

devanagari: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते । / सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥12.3॥
iast: ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate । / sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam ॥12.3॥
sayIt: yay tvak-SHA-ram a-nir-DAYSH-yam av-YAK-tam par-yoo-PAA-sa-tay / sar-vat-ra-GAM a-CHIN-tyam cha koo-ta-STHAM a-CHA-lam dhroo-VAM
translation: But those who worship the imperishable — the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the inconceivable, the unchanging, the immovable, the constant — (the sentence continues in 12.4).
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.3, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: This verse is the first half of a sentence completed in 12.4. Krishna now turns to the other kind of practitioner from Arjuna's question: those who worship not a personal form but the imperishable absolute. The string of adjectives — indefinable, unmanifest, everywhere, beyond thought, unchanging, immovable, constant — is itself a lesson in how hard this object of contemplation is to hold. Every word says what it is not, or what it never does. For someone building a daily practice, the verse honours the contemplative path while quietly showing why it demands so much: the mind is being asked to rest on something it cannot picture. Krishna's own assessment of that difficulty comes in 12.5.
reflection: What draws people toward a truth beyond every image?

translations.hi: परंतु जो अविनाशी की उपासना करते हैं — जो अनिर्वचनीय है, अव्यक्त, सर्वव्यापी, अचिन्त्य, अपरिवर्तनीय, अचल और ध्रुव — (वाक्य 12.4 में पूरा होता है)।

meanings.hi: यह श्लोक उस वाक्य का पहला आधा हिस्सा है जो 12.4 में पूरा होता है। कृष्ण अब अर्जुन के प्रश्न में आए दूसरे प्रकार के साधक की ओर मुड़ते हैं: वे जो किसी व्यक्तिगत रूप की नहीं, बल्कि अविनाशी परम तत्व की उपासना करते हैं। विशेषणों की यह शृंखला — अनिर्वचनीय, अव्यक्त, सर्वव्यापी, विचार से परे, अपरिवर्तनीय, अचल, ध्रुव — अपने आप में एक पाठ है कि चिंतन का यह विषय पकड़ में आना कितना कठिन है। हर शब्द बताता है कि वह क्या नहीं है, या क्या कभी नहीं करता। दैनिक अभ्यास गढ़ने वाले के लिए यह श्लोक चिंतन-मार्ग का सम्मान करता है, पर चुपचाप यह भी दिखाता है कि वह इतनी माँग क्यों करता है: मन से कहा जा रहा है कि वह किसी ऐसी चीज़ पर टिके जिसकी कोई तस्वीर नहीं बनती। इस कठिनाई पर कृष्ण का अपना आकलन 12.5 में आता है।

devanagari: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । / ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥12.4॥
iast: saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ । / te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ ॥12.4॥
sayIt: sam-ni-YAM-yen-dri-ya-GRAA-mam sar-VAT-ra sa-ma-BOOD-dha-yah / tay praap-noo-VAN-ti MAAM-ay-va sar-va-BHOO-ta-hi-tay ra-TAAH
translation: — those who fully restrain their senses, stay even-minded in every situation, and delight in the welfare of all beings — they too reach me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.4, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: in the welfare of all beings

meaning: Completing the sentence begun in 12.3, Krishna says that worshippers of the formless absolute also reach him — provided their contemplation is matched by conduct: senses restrained, mind even in every circumstance, and a genuine delight in the good of all beings. That last phrase matters most for daily life. The verse refuses to let formless meditation become private escape; the test of the practice is equanimity and active care for others. Both paths from Arjuna's question arrive at the same destination. Traditions gloss "they reach me" differently — Advaita reads it as realising the self that Krishna is, bhakti schools as attaining the Lord — but all agree the contemplative path, done fully, succeeds.
reflection: Whose good, beyond your own, will your practice serve today?

translations.hi: — जो अपनी सारी इंद्रियों को पूरी तरह संयम में रखते हैं, हर स्थिति में समबुद्धि रहते हैं और सभी प्राणियों के हित में रमे रहते हैं — वे भी मुझे ही पाते हैं।

meanings.hi: 12.3 में शुरू हुए वाक्य को पूरा करते हुए कृष्ण कहते हैं कि निराकार परम की उपासना करने वाले भी उन तक पहुँचते हैं — बशर्ते उनका चिंतन आचरण से मेल खाए: इंद्रियाँ संयमित हों, मन हर परिस्थिति में सम रहे, और सभी प्राणियों के भले में सच्चा आनंद हो। रोज़मर्रा के जीवन के लिए वही आख़िरी बात सबसे अहम है। श्लोक निराकार ध्यान को निजी पलायन नहीं बनने देता; अभ्यास की कसौटी है समता और दूसरों के लिए सक्रिय परवाह। अर्जुन के प्रश्न के दोनों मार्ग एक ही मंज़िल पर पहुँचते हैं। "वे मुझे पाते हैं" की व्याख्या परंपराओं में अलग है — अद्वैत इसे उस आत्म की अनुभूति मानता है जो कृष्ण हैं, भक्ति-परंपराएँ भगवान की प्राप्ति — पर सब मानते हैं कि पूरी निष्ठा से किया गया चिंतन-मार्ग सफल होता है।

devanagari: क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् । / अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥12.5॥
iast: kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām । / avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate ॥12.5॥
sayIt: KLAY-sho dhi-ka-ta-RAS-tay-shaam av-yak-TAA-sak-ta-CHAY-ta-saam / av-yak-TAA hi ga-TEER dooh-KHAM day-ha-vad-BHEER a-VAAP-ya-tay
translation: The struggle is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest, for a goal without form is hard for embodied beings to reach.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.5, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: whose minds are attached to the unmanifest

meaning: Krishna adds an honest caveat: the formless path works, but it is harder. We are embodied creatures — we think in images, love with senses, and anchor attention in what we can perceive. Asking the mind to rest on something without any form goes against that grain, so the struggle is greater. This is not a dismissal of contemplative practice; it is practical guidance about difficulty, like a trail map marking the steeper route. For a daily practice, the takeaway is permission: using a form, a name, an image, or a lamp flame is not a lesser method — it is the path suited to beings with bodies. Advaita traditions read the difficulty as provisional rather than a ranking of truths; bhakti traditions read it as pointing to devotion's superiority.
reflection: Where has the formless path felt hard for you — and what made it so?

translations.hi: जिनका मन अव्यक्त में लगा है, उनके लिए कठिनाई अधिक है; क्योंकि देहधारियों के लिए रूप-रहित लक्ष्य तक पहुँचना दुष्कर है।

meanings.hi: कृष्ण एक ईमानदार बात जोड़ते हैं: निराकार मार्ग काम करता है, पर वह ज़्यादा कठिन है। हम देहधारी प्राणी हैं — छवियों में सोचते हैं, इंद्रियों से प्रेम करते हैं और ध्यान उसी में टिकाते हैं जिसे महसूस कर सकें। मन से यह कहना कि वह बिना किसी रूप की चीज़ पर टिके, इस स्वभाव के विरुद्ध जाता है, इसलिए संघर्ष बड़ा है। यह चिंतन-साधना की उपेक्षा नहीं; यह कठिनाई के बारे में व्यावहारिक मार्गदर्शन है, जैसे नक्शे पर खड़ी चढ़ाई का निशान। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए संदेश एक अनुमति है: रूप, नाम, छवि या दीये की लौ का सहारा लेना कोई कमतर तरीका नहीं — वह देहधारियों के अनुकूल मार्ग है। अद्वैत परंपराएँ इस कठिनाई को सत्यों की श्रेणी नहीं, अस्थायी बाधा मानती हैं; भक्ति-परंपराएँ इसे भक्ति की श्रेष्ठता का संकेत पढ़ती हैं।

devanagari: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । / अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥12.6॥
iast: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ । / ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate ॥12.6॥
sayIt: yay too sar-VAA-ni kar-MAA-ni MA-yi san-NYAS-ya mat-pa-RAAH / a-nan-yay-NAI-va yo-GAY-na maam dhyaa-YAN-ta oo-PAA-sa-tay
translation: But those who dedicate all their actions to me, hold me as their highest aim, and worship me, meditating on me with undivided devotion — (the sentence continues in 12.7).
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.6, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: holding me as the highest aim

meaning: The first half of a sentence completed in 12.7, this verse describes the devotional alternative to the steep formless path. Three moves define it: dedicate every action to the divine rather than to personal gain, make that relationship your highest aim, and let attention rest on the divine without dividing it among competing refuges. Notice that the verse starts with action, not withdrawal — ordinary work continues, but its ownership changes hands. For a daily practice this is the most portable instruction in the chapter: you cannot always sit in meditation, but you can offer whatever you are already doing. What that offering earns is stated in the next verse.
reflection: What would it mean to hand today's worries over, fully?

translations.hi: परंतु जो अपने सारे कर्म मुझे समर्पित करके, मुझे ही परम लक्ष्य मानकर, अनन्य योग से मेरा ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं — (वाक्य 12.7 में पूरा होता है)।

meanings.hi: 12.7 में पूरे होने वाले वाक्य का यह पहला आधा हिस्सा उस भक्ति-विकल्प का वर्णन है जो खड़ी चढ़ाई वाले निराकार मार्ग के सामने रखा गया है। तीन कदम इसे परिभाषित करते हैं: हर कर्म निजी लाभ की बजाय ईश्वर को समर्पित करना, उस संबंध को अपना सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य बनाना, और ध्यान को कई प्रतिस्पर्धी सहारों में बाँटे बिना ईश्वर पर टिकने देना। ग़ौर कीजिए कि श्लोक की शुरुआत कर्म से होती है, संसार-त्याग से नहीं — सामान्य काम चलता रहता है, बस उसका स्वामित्व हाथ बदल लेता है। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए यह अध्याय का सबसे साथ ले चलने लायक निर्देश है: आप हर समय ध्यान में नहीं बैठ सकते, पर जो कर ही रहे हैं उसे अर्पित कर सकते हैं। इस अर्पण का फल अगले श्लोक में बताया गया है।

devanagari: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । / भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥12.7॥
iast: teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt । / bhavāmi nacirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām ॥12.7॥
sayIt: TAY-shaam a-HAM sa-mood-DHAR-taa mrit-yoo-sam-SAA-ra-saa-ga-RAAT / bha-VAA-mi na chi-RAAT PAAR-tha mai-YAA-vay-shi-ta-CHAY-ta-saam
translation: — for them, whose minds have entered into me, I soon become the rescuer from the ocean of death-bound existence, O Partha.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: the rescuer, the one who lifts up
from the ocean of death-bound worldly existence
of those whose minds have entered, are absorbed

meaning: Completing the sentence begun in 12.6, Krishna makes a promise: for those whose minds are absorbed in him, he himself becomes the rescuer from the ocean of samsara — and soon, not after lifetimes of effort. The image reverses the usual picture of spiritual work. On the formless path of 12.3–12.5, the practitioner climbs; here, the swimmer is lifted. The effort asked of the devotee is orientation — turning the mind toward the divine — while the crossing itself is described as God's act. For daily practice, this verse is the chapter's reassurance: the practice is not self-rescue but sustained trust. Bhakti traditions read this grace as central; Advaita readings frame the rescue as the removal of ignorance.
reflection: Where in your life are you waiting for help you could simply ask for?

translations.hi: — हे पार्थ, जिनका चित्त मुझमें समा गया है, उनके लिए मैं शीघ्र ही मृत्यु से बँधे संसार-सागर से उबारने वाला बन जाता हूँ।

meanings.hi: 12.6 में शुरू हुए वाक्य को पूरा करते हुए कृष्ण एक वचन देते हैं: जिनका मन उनमें रम गया है, उनके लिए वे स्वयं संसार-सागर से उबारने वाले बनते हैं — और शीघ्र, जन्मों की मेहनत के बाद नहीं। यह छवि आध्यात्मिक श्रम की आम तस्वीर को पलट देती है। 12.3–12.5 के निराकार मार्ग पर साधक चढ़ाई करता है; यहाँ तैरने वाले को उठा लिया जाता है। भक्त से जो प्रयास माँगा गया है वह है दिशा — मन को ईश्वर की ओर मोड़ना — जबकि पार कराना स्वयं ईश्वर का कर्म बताया गया है। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए यह श्लोक अध्याय का आश्वासन है: साधना आत्म-उद्धार नहीं, टिका हुआ भरोसा है। भक्ति-परंपराएँ इस कृपा को केंद्रीय मानती हैं; अद्वैत की व्याख्याएँ इस उद्धार को अज्ञान के हटने के रूप में देखती हैं।

devanagari: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । / निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥12.8॥
iast: mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya । / nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ॥12.8॥
sayIt: mai-YAY-va MA-na AA-dhats-va MA-yi BOOD-dhim ni-VAY-sha-ya / ni-va-SISH-ya-si mai-YAY-va A-ta OORD-hvam na san-sha-YAH
translation: Fix your mind on me alone; settle your understanding in me. From then on you will live in me — of this there is no doubt.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.8, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: you will dwell, you will live

meaning: This verse begins the chapter's famous ladder of practice. The first rung is the highest ask: fix both mind and intellect on the divine. The two words are distinct on purpose — manas is the feeling, wandering attention; buddhi is the judging, deciding faculty. Krishna asks for both: not just warm feeling that drifts elsewhere when deciding what to do, and not just intellectual conviction with no felt attention. When both settle in the same place, he says, you already dwell there — the goal is not deferred to another life. The next verses will lower the rung for those who cannot yet manage this, which is what makes the ladder humane.
reflection: Can you give the divine one undivided minute today?

translations.hi: अपना मन मुझमें ही स्थिर कर, अपनी बुद्धि मुझमें लगा दे। इसके बाद तू मुझमें ही निवास करेगा — इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं।

meanings.hi: यहाँ से अध्याय की प्रसिद्ध अभ्यास-सीढ़ी शुरू होती है। पहला पायदान सबसे ऊँची माँग है: मन और बुद्धि दोनों को ईश्वर पर टिका देना। दोनों शब्द जान-बूझकर अलग रखे गए हैं — मनस् वह भावुक, भटकता हुआ ध्यान है; बुद्धि परखने और निर्णय लेने वाली शक्ति। कृष्ण दोनों माँगते हैं: न सिर्फ़ ऐसी गर्म भावना जो निर्णय की घड़ी में कहीं और बह जाए, और न सिर्फ़ बौद्धिक सहमति जिसमें महसूस किया हुआ ध्यान न हो। जब दोनों एक ही जगह ठहर जाते हैं, तो कृष्ण कहते हैं, तुम वहीं निवास करने लगते हो — लक्ष्य किसी अगले जन्म तक टाला नहीं गया। अगले श्लोक उन लोगों के लिए पायदान नीचे लाएँगे जो अभी इतना नहीं कर पाते — यही बात इस सीढ़ी को मानवीय बनाती है।

devanagari: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । / अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनंजय ॥12.9॥
iast: atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram । / abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṃ dhanaṃjaya ॥12.9॥
sayIt: A-tha CHIT-tam sa-maa-DHAA-toom na shak-NO-shi MA-yi sthi-RAM / ab-hyaa-sa-yo-GAY-na TA-to maam ich-CHAAP-toom dha-nan-JA-ya
translation: But if you cannot hold your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of repeated practice, O Dhananjaya.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.9, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: through the yoga of repeated practice

meaning: The second rung of the ladder, and the one most daily practitioners actually stand on. If steady absorption is beyond you — and Krishna assumes without judgment that it may be — then practise repeatedly: abhyasa-yoga, the discipline of returning. The mind wanders; you bring it back; it wanders again; you bring it back again. That returning is not failure at the real practice — it is the real practice at this stage. This is the verse behind every habit-shaped devotion: a daily verse, a fixed time of prayer, a repeated name. Consistency substitutes for steadiness until, gradually, it produces it. The instruction is warmly matter-of-fact: inability is met with a method, not a rebuke.
reflection: What small, repeated practice could carry you when focus fails?

translations.hi: पर यदि तू अपना चित्त मुझ पर स्थिर नहीं रख पाता, तो हे धनंजय, अभ्यास-योग के द्वारा मुझे पाने की इच्छा कर।

meanings.hi: सीढ़ी का दूसरा पायदान — और वही, जिस पर ज़्यादातर दैनिक साधक असल में खड़े हैं। यदि स्थिर तल्लीनता तुम्हारे बस में नहीं — और कृष्ण बिना कोई फ़ैसला सुनाए मान लेते हैं कि हो सकता है न हो — तो बार-बार अभ्यास करो: अभ्यास-योग, लौटने का अनुशासन। मन भटकता है; तुम उसे वापस लाते हो; वह फिर भटकता है; तुम फिर लाते हो। यह लौटना असली साधना में असफलता नहीं — इस चरण पर यही असली साधना है। आदत की शक्ल वाली हर भक्ति के पीछे यही श्लोक है: रोज़ एक श्लोक, प्रार्थना का तय समय, दोहराया हुआ नाम। नियमितता स्थिरता की जगह लेती है, जब तक धीरे-धीरे वही उसे जन्म न दे दे। निर्देश का स्वर सहज और स्नेह भरा है: असमर्थता का उत्तर एक विधि है, फटकार नहीं।

devanagari: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । / मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥12.10॥
iast: abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava । / madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvansiddhimavāpsyasi ॥12.10॥
sayIt: ab-HYAA-say pya-sa-MAR-tho si mat-kar-ma-pa-ra-MO BHA-va / ma-dar-THAM a-pi kar-MAA-ni KOOR-van SID-dhim a-VAAP-sya-si
translation: If you cannot even manage this practice, then devote yourself to working for me; even by doing actions for my sake you will reach fulfilment.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.10, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: devoted above all to work for me

meaning: The ladder descends another rung. If even structured, repeated practice is beyond you right now, Krishna offers something anyone can do: act for his sake. No meditation posture, no fixed discipline — just take the work already in your hands and dedicate it. Cook, drive, care for someone, do your job, but do it as an offering rather than only for yourself. The verse promises that this alone leads to fulfilment, because the reorientation of motive is itself transformative. For someone starting a daily practice, this is the most forgiving entry point in the Gita: begin where you are, with what you are already doing, and let dedication do the early work that concentration cannot yet do.
reflection: What ordinary work today could you do as an offering?

translations.hi: यदि तू यह अभ्यास भी नहीं कर पाता, तो मेरे लिए कर्म करने में लग जा; मेरे लिए कर्म करते हुए भी तू सिद्धि पा लेगा।

meanings.hi: सीढ़ी एक पायदान और उतरती है। यदि इस समय व्यवस्थित, दोहराया हुआ अभ्यास भी बस के बाहर है, तो कृष्ण कुछ ऐसा देते हैं जो कोई भी कर सकता है: उनके लिए कर्म करो। न ध्यान की मुद्रा, न बँधा हुआ अनुशासन — बस जो काम पहले से हाथ में है, उसे समर्पित कर दो। खाना बनाओ, गाड़ी चलाओ, किसी की देखभाल करो, अपनी नौकरी करो — पर केवल अपने लिए नहीं, एक अर्पण की तरह। श्लोक वचन देता है कि इतने भर से सिद्धि मिलती है, क्योंकि इरादे का यह नया रुख़ अपने आप में रूपांतर लाता है। दैनिक अभ्यास शुरू करने वाले के लिए यह गीता का सबसे उदार प्रवेश-द्वार है: जहाँ हो वहीं से शुरू करो, जो कर रहे हो उसी से, और शुरुआती काम समर्पण को करने दो — वह काम जो एकाग्रता अभी नहीं कर पाती।

devanagari: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । / सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥12.11॥
iast: athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāśritaḥ । / sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān ॥12.11॥
sayIt: a-thai-ta-dap-ya-SHAK-toh-si KAR-tum mad-YO-ga-MAASH-ri-tah / sar-va-kar-ma-pha-la-TYAA-gam TA-tah KU-ru ya-TAAT-ma-vaan
translation: And if even this is beyond you, then, taking refuge in union with me, give up the fruits of all your actions with a disciplined mind.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.11, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: the giving up of the fruits of all actions

meaning: This verse closes the ladder Krishna builds across 12.8–11. If fixing the mind wholly on him is out of reach, and steady practice too, and even working for his sake feels like too much, one door is always open: keep doing your work, and let go of its results. That release, made with some self-restraint, is itself a full spiritual practice, and it needs no special skill, free time, or temperament. Commentators read the ladder differently — Advaita teachers often see descending steps suited to different capacities, while Vaishnava commentators tend to read them as alternative routes — but all agree that relinquishing results is a door open to everyone, which is exactly what makes it a workable daily discipline.
reflection: What outcome are you ready to surrender tonight?

translations.hi: और यदि यह भी तेरे बस में नहीं, तो मेरे योग का आश्रय लेकर, संयमित मन से सब कर्मों के फल का त्याग कर।

meanings.hi: यह श्लोक 12.8–11 में बनी कृष्ण की सीढ़ी को पूरा करता है। यदि मन को पूरी तरह उन पर टिकाना पहुँच से बाहर है, स्थिर अभ्यास भी, और उनके लिए काम करना भी बहुत लगता है, तो एक द्वार सदा खुला है: अपना काम करते रहो और उसके परिणाम छोड़ दो। थोड़े आत्म-संयम के साथ किया गया यह त्याग अपने आप में एक पूरी आध्यात्मिक साधना है, और इसके लिए कोई विशेष कौशल, खाली समय या स्वभाव नहीं चाहिए। टीकाकार इस सीढ़ी को अलग-अलग पढ़ते हैं — अद्वैत आचार्य प्रायः इन्हें भिन्न क्षमताओं के अनुसार उतरते चरण मानते हैं, जबकि वैष्णव टीकाकार इन्हें वैकल्पिक रास्ते — पर सब सहमत हैं कि फल का त्याग सबके लिए खुला द्वार है, और यही उसे एक व्यावहारिक दैनिक अनुशासन बनाता है।

devanagari: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते । / ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥12.12॥
iast: śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate । / dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram ॥12.12॥
sayIt: SHRAY-yo hi GYAA-na-mab-YAA-saaj GYAA-naad DHYAA-nam vi-SHISH-ya-tay / DHYAA-naat kar-ma-pha-la-TYAA-gas TYAA-gaach CHAAN-ti-ra-nan-ta-ram
translation: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruits of action is better than meditation — for peace follows immediately upon that giving up.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.12, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: the giving up of the fruits of action

meaning: Krishna ranks the inner disciplines: knowledge is better than rote practice, meditation better than knowledge, and letting go of the results of action better still — because peace follows it immediately. For a daily practice this is encouraging rather than demanding. The step named highest here is not a rare attainment reserved for experts; it is a decision available today: do the task, release the outcome, and notice the quiet that follows. Commentators differ on how literally to take the ranking — some read it as praise of relinquishment meant to encourage the struggling practitioner rather than a fixed hierarchy of paths — so hold the sequence lightly and keep the practical point: relinquishment brings peace without delay.
reflection: What would one moment of true letting-go feel like today?

translations.hi: अभ्यास से ज्ञान श्रेष्ठ है; ज्ञान से ध्यान बढ़कर है; और ध्यान से कर्मफल का त्याग — क्योंकि त्याग के तुरंत बाद शांति आती है।

meanings.hi: कृष्ण भीतरी अनुशासनों की श्रेणी बताते हैं: रटे हुए अभ्यास से ज्ञान बेहतर, ज्ञान से ध्यान, और कर्म के फलों को छोड़ देना उससे भी बढ़कर — क्योंकि उसके तुरंत बाद शांति आती है। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए यह माँग नहीं, हौसला है। यहाँ जिसे सर्वोच्च कहा गया है वह विशेषज्ञों के लिए आरक्षित कोई दुर्लभ उपलब्धि नहीं; वह आज ही उपलब्ध एक निर्णय है: काम करो, परिणाम छोड़ो, और पीछे-पीछे आती शांति को महसूस करो। इस क्रम को कितना शाब्दिक लिया जाए, इस पर टीकाकारों में मतभेद है — कुछ इसे मार्गों की स्थायी श्रेणी नहीं, बल्कि जूझते साधक का हौसला बढ़ाने के लिए त्याग की प्रशंसा मानते हैं — इसलिए क्रम को हल्के से पकड़िए और व्यावहारिक बात याद रखिए: त्याग बिना देर किए शांति लाता है।

devanagari: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । / निर्ममो निरहंकारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥12.13॥
iast: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca । / nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī ॥12.13॥
sayIt: ad-VESH-taa sar-va-bhoo-TAA-naam MAI-trah KA-ru-na AY-va cha / nir-MA-mo ni-ra-han-KAA-rah sa-ma-DUH-kha-su-khah KSHA-mee
translation: One who bears no ill will toward any being, who is friendly and compassionate, free of possessiveness and self-importance, the same in sorrow and joy, and patient —
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.13, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: free of ego, without the conceit of "I"
the same in sorrow and joy

meaning: Here begins the portrait Krishna paints, through verse 20, of the devotee who is dear to him — and it opens as a sentence completed in 12.14. It starts not with feats but with gentleness: no ill will toward any being, friendliness, compassion, freedom from "me" and "mine", evenness in joy and sorrow, patience. Notice that every quality is relational; this is devotion measured by how we meet whatever crosses our path. For a daily practice, the verse offers a simple evening check-in: was I friendly today, and what am I still gripping as "mine"? Across Vaishnava, Advaita, and other readings these verses are received remarkably alike — a shared ideal rather than a point of dispute.
reflection: Toward whom can you practise friendliness without conditions today?

translations.hi: जो किसी भी प्राणी से द्वेष नहीं रखता, जो मैत्रीपूर्ण और करुणामय है, ममता और अहंकार से मुक्त, सुख-दुख में सम और क्षमाशील है —

meanings.hi: यहाँ से वह चित्र शुरू होता है जिसे कृष्ण श्लोक 20 तक खींचते हैं — उस भक्त का, जो उन्हें प्रिय है — और यह एक ऐसे वाक्य के रूप में खुलता है जो 12.14 में पूरा होता है। शुरुआत करतबों से नहीं, कोमलता से होती है: किसी प्राणी से द्वेष नहीं, मैत्री, करुणा, "मैं" और "मेरे" से मुक्ति, सुख-दुख में समता, धैर्य। ध्यान दीजिए कि हर गुण संबंधों का है; यह वह भक्ति है जो इस बात से मापी जाती है कि हम अपने रास्ते में आने वाली हर चीज़ से कैसे मिलते हैं। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए श्लोक शाम की एक सीधी जाँच देता है: क्या मैं आज मैत्रीपूर्ण रहा, और किस चीज़ को अब भी "मेरा" कहकर जकड़े हुए हूँ? वैष्णव, अद्वैत और अन्य पाठों में ये श्लोक लगभग एक-से भाव से ग्रहण किए जाते हैं — विवाद का नहीं, साझा आदर्श का विषय।

devanagari: संतुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । / मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥12.14॥
iast: saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ । / mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ॥12.14॥
sayIt: san-TUSH-tah sa-ta-tam YO-gee ya-TAAT-maa dri-dha-NISH-cha-yah / may-YAR-pi-ta-ma-no-BUD-dhir yo mad-BHAK-tah sa may PRI-yah
translation: — that yogi who is always content, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to me — that devotee of mine is dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.14, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: the yogi, one joined in practice
that one is dear to me

meaning: Completing the sentence begun in 12.13, the portrait turns inward: contentment that does not depend on circumstances, steadiness, self-control, firm resolve, and a mind and understanding quietly offered to the divine. The word satatam — "always" — matters: contentment here is a cultivated habit, not a lucky mood. For someone building a daily practice, this verse describes what regularity is for. Small, repeated acts of attention slowly firm up resolve, and offering becomes a reflex rather than an occasion. Nothing here requires leaving home or work; the offering happens in the mind and heart. Commentarial traditions place different weight on "offered to me" — the personal Krishna or the supreme reality — but the practice described is the same.
reflection: What is one contentment you keep overlooking?

translations.hi: — जो योगी सदा संतुष्ट है, संयमी और दृढ़ निश्चय वाला, जिसने अपने मन और बुद्धि मुझे अर्पित कर दिए हैं — मेरा वह भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।

meanings.hi: 12.13 में शुरू हुए वाक्य को पूरा करते हुए चित्र भीतर की ओर मुड़ता है: परिस्थितियों पर न टिका संतोष, स्थिरता, आत्म-संयम, दृढ़ निश्चय, और चुपचाप ईश्वर को अर्पित मन-बुद्धि। "सततम्" — सदा — शब्द महत्वपूर्ण है: यहाँ संतोष एक साधी हुई आदत है, कोई भाग्यशाली मनोदशा नहीं। दैनिक अभ्यास गढ़ने वाले के लिए यह श्लोक बताता है कि नियमितता आख़िर किसलिए है। ध्यान के छोटे, दोहराए हुए काम धीरे-धीरे निश्चय को पक्का करते हैं, और अर्पण किसी ख़ास अवसर की जगह सहज वृत्ति बन जाता है। इसमें घर या काम छोड़ने की कोई शर्त नहीं; अर्पण मन और हृदय में होता है। "मुझे अर्पित" पर टीका-परंपराएँ अलग-अलग ज़ोर देती हैं — व्यक्तिगत कृष्ण या परम तत्व — पर वर्णित साधना एक ही है।

devanagari: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । / हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥12.15॥
iast: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ । / harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ॥12.15॥
sayIt: yas-MAAN-nod-vi-ja-tay LO-ko lo-KAAN-nod-vi-ja-tay cha yah / har-SHAA-mar-sha-bha-YOD-vay-gair MUK-to yah sa cha may PRI-yah
translation: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from excitement, resentment, fear, and anxiety — that one too is dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.15, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: does not shrink, is not disturbed
that one too is dear to me

meaning: This verse looks at devotion from the outside in. The dear devotee is someone the world does not shrink from, and who does not shrink from the world: not a source of agitation for others, and not agitated by them. Four disturbances are named — elation, resentment, fear, anxiety — the churn that tosses an ordinary day about. It is a gentle and slightly startling measure of progress: how do people feel around you? For daily practice, it invites noticing which of the four visits most often and meeting it with a breath rather than a reaction. Commentarial traditions read this image of mutual non-disturbance in essentially the same warm spirit.
reflection: Do people relax around you? What would make it so?

translations.hi: जिससे लोग व्याकुल नहीं होते और जो लोगों से व्याकुल नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, खीझ, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह भी मुझे प्रिय है।

meanings.hi: यह श्लोक भक्ति को बाहर से भीतर की ओर देखता है। प्रिय भक्त वह है जिससे संसार नहीं सिकुड़ता और जो संसार से नहीं सिकुड़ता: न दूसरों की बेचैनी का कारण, न उनसे बेचैन। चार विक्षोभ गिनाए गए हैं — उत्तेजना, खीझ, भय, चिंता — वही मथानी जो एक साधारण दिन को उलट-पलट देती है। यह प्रगति की एक कोमल और थोड़ी चौंकाने वाली कसौटी है: लोग आपके आसपास कैसा महसूस करते हैं? दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए यह न्योता है कि ध्यान दें — चारों में से कौन सबसे अधिक आता है — और उसे प्रतिक्रिया की जगह एक साँस से मिलें। आपसी अ-विक्षोभ की इस छवि को टीका-परंपराएँ लगभग इसी स्नेह भरे भाव से पढ़ती हैं।

devanagari: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । / सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥12.16॥
iast: anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ । / sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ॥12.16॥
sayIt: a-na-PAYK-shah SHU-chir DAK-sha u-daa-SEE-no ga-ta-VYA-thah / sar-VAA-ram-bha-pa-ri-TYAA-gee yo mad-BHAK-tah sa may PRI-yah
translation: One who wants nothing, who is pure, capable, impartial, and untroubled, who has given up all self-interested undertakings — that devotee of mine is dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.16, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: impartial, sitting apart from taking sides
who has given up all (self-interested) undertakings

meaning: The qualities here are strikingly practical: wanting nothing extra, cleanliness inner and outer, capability in what one does, impartiality, freedom from anguish, and letting go of self-driven schemes. "Giving up all undertakings" cannot mean idleness — the Gita has spent chapters insisting on action — and commentators across traditions vary in nuance here: most take it as dropping projects driven purely by personal gain, or dropping the anxious sense of being the doer, rather than dropping work itself. For a daily practice, the pairing of dakṣa (skilful) with udāsīna (unattached) is the heart of the verse: do your work well, and hold it lightly. Those two together, not either alone, mark the dear devotee.
reflection: What expectation could you set down to travel lighter today?

translations.hi: जो अपेक्षा-रहित है, पवित्र, दक्ष, तटस्थ और व्यथा से मुक्त है, जिसने सारे स्वार्थ-प्रेरित आरंभ छोड़ दिए हैं — मेरा वह भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।

meanings.hi: यहाँ गिनाए गुण बेहद व्यावहारिक हैं: कुछ अतिरिक्त न चाहना, भीतर-बाहर की शुद्धता, अपने काम में दक्षता, तटस्थता, व्यथा से मुक्ति, और अपने ही स्वार्थ से चलने वाली योजनाओं को छोड़ देना। "सारे आरंभ छोड़ना" निठल्लापन नहीं हो सकता — गीता कई अध्यायों से कर्म पर ज़ोर देती आई है — और यहाँ टीकाकारों की बारीकियाँ अलग-अलग हैं: अधिकांश इसे केवल निजी लाभ से प्रेरित परियोजनाओं को छोड़ना, या कर्ता होने के तनाव भरे भाव को छोड़ना मानते हैं, काम को नहीं। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए दक्ष (कुशल) और उदासीन (अनासक्त) की जोड़ी ही इस श्लोक का हृदय है: अपना काम अच्छे से करो, और उसे हल्के से थामो। ये दोनों साथ-साथ — कोई एक अकेला नहीं — प्रिय भक्त की पहचान हैं।

devanagari: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । / शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥12.17॥
iast: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati । / śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ ॥12.17॥
sayIt: yo na HRISH-ya-ti na DVESH-ti na SHO-cha-ti na KAANK-sha-ti / shu-BHAA-shu-bha-pa-ri-TYAA-gee bhak-ti-MAAN yah sa may PRI-yah
translation: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both the pleasant and the unpleasant — that devoted one is dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.17, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: who lets go of both the pleasant and the unpleasant
that one is dear to me

meaning: Four quiet freedoms: not clinging to elation when things go well, not hating, not grieving, not craving. The verse is not asking for a flat, feelingless life; it points at the spikes and crashes that toss the mind around, and at the peace of letting both the pleasant and the unpleasant pass through without gripping either. For daily practice this yields a usable evening question: what did I grip today, and what did I push away? Devotion — bhaktimān — is named as what makes the letting-go possible, because the heart is resting on something steadier than events. Commentators across traditions read this verse in essentially the same spirit, with little material disagreement.
reflection: What loss are you gripping that is asking to be released?

translations.hi: जो न हर्ष में बहता है, न द्वेष करता है, न शोक करता है, न कामना करता है, जिसने शुभ और अशुभ दोनों को छोड़ दिया है — वह भक्तिमान मुझे प्रिय है।

meanings.hi: चार शांत मुक्तियाँ: काम बन जाने पर उल्लास से न चिपकना, द्वेष न करना, शोक न करना, लालसा न करना। श्लोक किसी सपाट, भावहीन जीवन की माँग नहीं करता; वह उन उछालों और गिरावटों की ओर इशारा करता है जो मन को झकझोरती हैं, और उस शांति की ओर, जो सुखद और अप्रिय दोनों को बिना जकड़े गुज़र जाने देने में है। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए इससे शाम का एक काम का सवाल निकलता है: आज मैंने किसे जकड़ा, और किसे धकेला? जो यह छोड़ना संभव बनाती है, उसका नाम है भक्ति — भक्तिमान — क्योंकि हृदय घटनाओं से अधिक स्थिर किसी चीज़ पर टिका है। इस श्लोक को टीकाकार परंपराओं के आर-पार लगभग एक ही भाव से पढ़ते हैं; कोई बड़ा मतभेद नहीं।

devanagari: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥12.18॥
iast: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ । / śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ ॥12.18॥
sayIt: SA-mah SHA-trow cha MI-tray cha ta-THAA maa-NAA-pa-maa-na-yoh / shee-TOSH-na-su-kha-DUH-khay-shu SA-mah SAN-ga-vi-VAR-ji-tah
translation: One who is the same toward enemy and friend, the same in honour and disgrace, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from clinging —
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.18, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: in cold and heat, pleasure and pain

meaning: Evenness, tested exactly where it is hardest: enemy and friend, honour and disgrace, cold and heat, pleasure and pain. The verse pairs outer conditions we cannot control with the inner responses we slowly can, and it runs on into 12.19 as a single sentence. The root of the list is saṅga-vivarjitaḥ, "free from clinging": when we stop needing situations to arrange themselves a certain way, the same steadiness becomes available in all of them. For a daily practitioner this is not a demand to feel nothing — it is an invitation to notice where your evenness breaks first, often at honour and disgrace, and to practise gently there. Traditions read this verse in broadly the same way.
reflection: Where can you stay steady today — in praise or in blame?

translations.hi: जो शत्रु और मित्र के प्रति सम है, मान और अपमान में भी वैसा ही, सर्दी-गर्मी और सुख-दुख में सम, और आसक्ति से मुक्त है —

meanings.hi: समता — और उसकी परीक्षा ठीक वहाँ, जहाँ वह सबसे कठिन है: शत्रु और मित्र, मान और अपमान, सर्दी और गर्मी, सुख और दुख। श्लोक उन बाहरी स्थितियों को, जिन्हें हम नियंत्रित नहीं कर सकते, उन भीतरी प्रतिक्रियाओं के साथ रखता है जिन्हें धीरे-धीरे कर सकते हैं, और यह 12.19 में एक ही वाक्य के रूप में आगे बढ़ता है। सूची की जड़ है "सङ्गविवर्जितः" — आसक्ति से मुक्त: जब हमें स्थितियों के किसी ख़ास ढंग से सजने की ज़रूरत नहीं रहती, तो वही स्थिरता सब स्थितियों में उपलब्ध हो जाती है। दैनिक साधक के लिए यह कुछ भी महसूस न करने की माँग नहीं — यह न्योता है कि देखें, आपकी समता सबसे पहले कहाँ टूटती है — अक्सर मान-अपमान पर — और वहीं कोमलता से अभ्यास करें। परंपराएँ इस श्लोक को मोटे तौर पर एक ही तरह पढ़ती हैं।

devanagari: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् । / अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥12.19॥
iast: tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yena kenacit । / aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ ॥12.19॥
sayIt: tul-ya-nin-DAA-stu-tir MOW-nee san-TUSH-to YAY-na KAY-na-chit / a-ni-KAY-tah sthi-ra-MA-tir bhak-ti-MAAN may PRI-yo NA-rah
translation: — alike in blame and praise, sparing with speech, content with whatever comes, at home anywhere, steady in mind, and full of devotion — that person is dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.19, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: the same in blame and praise
with whatever comes, with anything at all
without a fixed home, at home anywhere

meaning: This verse completes the sentence begun in 12.18: alike in blame and praise, sparing with speech, content with whatever comes, at home anywhere, steady in mind, full of devotion — such a person is dear to Krishna. Two words are read differently across traditions: renunciant readings take aniketaḥ ("homeless") as describing the wandering monk, while householder-oriented readings take it inwardly, as not being possessed by one's possessions or address. Both agree on the core — an identity resting in devotion rather than in reputation or comfort. For daily practice, blame-and-praise is the accessible edge: notice how each one lands in you, and how long it stays.
reflection: What is your silence like — empty, or full?

translations.hi: — जो निंदा और स्तुति में समान है, वाणी में संयमी, जो कुछ मिल जाए उसमें संतुष्ट, किसी ठिकाने से न बँधा हुआ, स्थिर बुद्धि वाला और भक्ति से भरा — वह मनुष्य मुझे प्रिय है।

meanings.hi: यह श्लोक 12.18 में शुरू हुआ वाक्य पूरा करता है: निंदा-स्तुति में समान, वाणी में संयमी, जो मिले उसमें संतुष्ट, कहीं भी घर जैसा, स्थिर मन और भक्ति से भरा — ऐसा व्यक्ति कृष्ण को प्रिय है। दो शब्दों को परंपराएँ अलग-अलग पढ़ती हैं: संन्यास-केंद्रित पाठ "अनिकेतः" (गृहहीन) को घुमक्कड़ संन्यासी का वर्णन मानते हैं, जबकि गृहस्थ-उन्मुख पाठ इसे भीतर की बात मानते हैं — अपनी संपत्ति या पते के क़ब्ज़े में न होना। मूल पर दोनों सहमत हैं — एक ऐसी पहचान जो प्रतिष्ठा या सुविधा पर नहीं, भक्ति पर टिकी है। दैनिक अभ्यास के लिए निंदा-और-स्तुति ही सबसे सुलभ किनारा है: देखिए, हर एक आप में कैसे उतरती है, और कितनी देर ठहरती है।

devanagari: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते । / श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥12.20॥
iast: ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate । / śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ ॥12.20॥
sayIt: yay tu dhar-MYAAM-ri-ta-mi-dam ya-THOK-tam par-yu-PAA-sa-tay / shrad-da-DHAA-naa mat-pa-ra-MAA bhak-TAAS-tay TEE-va may pri-YAAH
translation: But those who honour this nectar of dharma as it has been taught, full of faith and holding me as the highest — those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 12.20, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: nectar of dharma, this life-giving teaching in accord with dharma
honour and follow with devoted attention

meaning: The chapter's closing verse gathers everything before it. Krishna calls the teaching of verses 13–19 dharmyāmṛtam — a nectar of dharma — and says that those who honour it with faith, holding him as the highest, are exceedingly dear to him. Two words carry the weight: śraddadhānāḥ, full of trust, and paryupāsate, which suggests devoted, ongoing attention rather than one-time agreement. That is precisely what a daily practice is — returning, with faith, to the same teaching until it soaks in. The verse is warmly received across traditions as the seal of the bhakti chapter, though commentators vary in how strongly they weight faith versus exclusive surrender.
reflection: Which of these qualities is quietly already yours?

translations.hi: परंतु जो श्रद्धा से भरे हुए, मुझे ही परम मानते हुए, इस धर्ममय अमृत का — जैसा कहा गया है वैसा ही — आदरपूर्वक पालन करते हैं, वे भक्त मुझे अत्यंत प्रिय हैं।

meanings.hi: अध्याय का समापन-श्लोक अपने से पहले की सारी बातें समेट लेता है। कृष्ण श्लोक 13–19 की शिक्षा को "धर्म्यामृतम्" — धर्म का अमृत — कहते हैं, और कहते हैं कि जो श्रद्धा के साथ, उन्हें परम मानकर इसका आदरपूर्वक पालन करते हैं, वे उन्हें अत्यंत प्रिय हैं। दो शब्द इसका भार उठाते हैं: "श्रद्दधानाः" — भरोसे से भरे — और "पर्युपासते", जो एक बार की सहमति नहीं, बल्कि समर्पित, निरंतर ध्यान का संकेत देता है। दैनिक अभ्यास ठीक यही तो है — श्रद्धा के साथ उसी शिक्षा की ओर बार-बार लौटना, जब तक वह भीतर न उतर जाए। भक्ति-अध्याय की मुहर के रूप में यह श्लोक सभी परंपराओं में स्नेह से ग्रहण किया जाता है, हालाँकि श्रद्धा बनाम अनन्य शरणागति पर टीकाकारों का ज़ोर अलग-अलग है।

devanagari: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । / मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥15.7॥
iast: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ । / manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati ॥15.7॥
sayIt: ma-my-VAAM-sho jee-va-LOH-kay jee-va-BHOO-tah sa-NAA-ta-nah / ma-nah-shush-TAA-neen-dri-YAA-ni pra-kri-ti-STAA-ni KAR-sha-ti
translation: An eternal part of my very self, having become the living soul in the world of the living, draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which rest in nature.
source: Bhagavad Gita 15.7, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: in the world of the living
with the mind as the sixth

meaning: A statement of identity before anything else: the living soul in you is an eternal portion of the divine — not a product of matter, not an accident. That portion, embodied, gathers up the five senses and the mind as a sixth instrument, all borrowed from nature, and works through them. How literally to take "portion" is a genuine dividing line between schools: Advaita reads the part-language as a manner of speaking about the one undivided Self, while Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita hold the individual soul to be really distinct and eternally related to God. All agree on the practical weight: what looks out through your eyes is older and more dignified than any of the day's troubles.
reflection: If the one looking out through your senses is an eternal portion of the divine, how does that change what today's problems weigh?

devanagari: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । / स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥18.46॥
iast: yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam । / svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ ॥18.46॥
sayIt: ya-TAH pra-VRIT-teer bhoo-TAA-naam YAY-na SAR-vum i-DUM ta-tum / sva-kar-ma-NAA ta-mubh-YARCH-ya SID-dhim VIN-da-ti MAA-na-vah
translation: By worshipping, through one's own work, the one from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains fulfilment.
source: Bhagavad Gita 18.46, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: Your own work — not someone else's more impressive work — can itself be the act of worship. The verse names its object carefully: the one from whom all beings flow and who pervades everything, so no workplace and no trade is outside the shrine. In its chapter context sva-karma meant the duty of one's station; the enduring principle is that fulfilment comes not from swapping your work for a holier-looking one but from converting the work you actually have into offering. Read alongside 18.47, which says your own dharma done imperfectly beats another's done well. For daily practice: today's tasks, done with care and dedicated upward, are the liturgy.
reflection: What would change about today's work if you treated it as your form of worship?

devanagari: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया । / विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥18.63॥
iast: iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā । / vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru ॥18.63॥
sayIt: i-ti tay GYAA-na-MAAKH-yaa-tum gooh-YAAD gooh-ya-ta-rum ma-YAA / vi-mrish-YIGH-ta-da-SHAY-shay-na ya-THAYCH-cha-si ta-THAA koo-roo
translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than secrecy itself. Reflect on it fully — and then do as you choose.
source: Bhagavad Gita 18.63, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review
meaning: After seventeen chapters of teaching, Krishna does something remarkable: he stops teaching. The entire discourse ends not with a command but with "reflect on it fully, then do as you choose" — yathecchasi tathā kuru. The teacher who could compel instead hands the decision back, making Arjuna's choice, and the reader's, genuinely free. Tradition treasures this as the model of how sacred knowledge is transmitted: offered completely, never forced. The two conditions matter as much as the freedom — reflect (don't react), and reflect fully (aśeṣeṇa, leaving nothing out). For daily practice it is a discipline for decisions: gather the wisdom, think it all the way through, then own your choice.
reflection: Which pending decision have you been waiting for someone else to make — and what would choosing it fully, after honest reflection, look like?

devanagari: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । / मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥18.65॥
iast: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru । / māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me ॥18.65॥
sayIt: mun-ma-NAA BHA-va mud-BHUK-toh mud-YAA-jee maam na-mus-KOO-roo / maa-may-VIGH-shya-si SUT-yum tay pra-ti-JAA-nay pri-YO-si may
translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer worship to me, bow to me — and you will come to me. This I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
source: Bhagavad Gita 18.65, Sanskrit Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA, https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE/%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%AF%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%83; translation: Dharma Daily draft, pending review

words.meaning: one who offers worship to me

meaning: The first line repeats 9.34 word for word — think of me, love me, worship me, bow to me — but what is new here changes the temperature of the whole teaching. Krishna adds a personal oath: satyaṃ te pratijāne, "I promise you truly," and then a reason: "you are dear to me." The relationship the Gita has been describing is not one-directional; the devotion flows back. Devotional traditions read this verse, beside 18.66, as the heart of the Gita's final teaching. For daily practice, notice that the instruction is fourfold and small — a thought, a feeling, an act, a bow — and that it is spoken to someone already loved.
reflection: How would your practice feel today if you began from being already dear, rather than trying to become worthy?

meaning: The Gita's final instruction, and its most debated. What "abandoning all dharmas" means genuinely divides the great commentarial traditions, and no single reading is the settled one. The Shrivaishnava tradition receives this as the charama shloka — the ultimate verse — teaching prapatti: complete surrender to the Lord as itself the way, with the divine promise doing the saving. Advaita reads the abandonment through renunciation and knowledge: the one who knows the Self stands beyond all action and its duties. Dvaita reads it differently again, as performing all dharma in surrender to Vishnu rather than discarding duty. What every reading shares is the ending: refuge is offered, the burden is lifted — mā śucaḥ, do not grieve.
reflection: What are you carrying alone that this verse invites you to set down and entrust?
